The three PRs this seat has in flight are `plugin-calendar` (#8027, enqueued), `plugin-tree` + test fixtures (#8030, enqueued), `plugin-charts` + `app-shell` (#8034, draft) — all disjoint from this card. ⛔ `packages/app-shell`'s own `ObjectView` is a **different component** (#7483) and is out of surface. No sibling card asserts a pin this card's behaviour would flip.

## ⭐ Clause-② is `no` BY CONSTRUCTION, and the stop-condition below is what makes it true

Read the card: it says the measurement decides which lane may take this. That is right, and it is why this dispatch is **bounded so that only one of the two branches can be executed here**.

```
packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:231-234   (JSDoc)  "If not provided, falls back to SchemaRendererProvider context."
packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:235       dataSource: DataSource;      <- required, no `?`
```
*(re-measured by this seat on `origin/main` `a9e6f04`, 2026-09-06T12:06Z — the card quotes no line numbers)*

**First, measure — this is the whole card:** does `ObjectView` actually consult `SchemaRendererProvider` context when `dataSource` is absent? Read it; ⛔ do not infer it from the prose.

**Branch A — the TYPE is right, the prose is stale.** Delete the false sentence (and fix any sibling prose repeating it). A comment deletion moves no accept set ⇒ `Clause-②: no` ⇒ finish the card, changeset per the repo's rules. ⚠️ Say in the PR body **what the component does instead** when `dataSource` is absent, because "the prose was wrong" is not by itself a description of the behaviour.

**Branch B — the JSDOC is right, the component really does fall back.** ⛔ **STOP AND REPORT. Do not implement it.** Making a required published prop optional **widens a published accept set** — that is `Clause-②: yes`, and by the mechanical boundary test a widening sits on the **manual floor**: it is the maintainer's call, not a dev's and not this seat's. Return `status: needs_decision` with the measurement, and this seat files it to the decision box. ⛔ A PR that makes the prop optional will be refused however good it is.

⇒ Whichever branch the measurement picks, **this dispatch never changes an accept set**, which is why it is `no` and why default-judgement tier is correct.

## PM mechanism assumptions — ⛔ measure, and I expect to be checked

1. ⭐ **I think Branch A is the answer, and I may be wrong.** `:786` reads `if (!dataSource || !schema.objectName) return;` and `:668` `if (!dataSource?.onMutation ...)` — the component appears to *guard* against an absent `dataSource` by doing nothing, ⛔ not by resolving one from context. I grep'd no context read for it. **That is a hint, not a measurement** — a fallback could be threaded in a hook (`useSettledSchema` at `:653`, or a wrapper) rather than at these sites. Prove it either way.
2. A third possibility the card does not list: the fallback may exist but be **dead** — e.g. resolved into a variable nothing downstream uses. If so, say so plainly; that is neither branch and it changes the disposition.
3. ⚠️ If the answer differs between the exported `ObjectView` and its internal render path, report the split rather than picking one.

## Boundaries

⛔ `packages/app-shell`'s `ObjectView` (typed `any` throughout) is **#7483**, a different component and a different defect — out of scope, ⛔ do not fold it in. ⛔ Do not "improve" the props surface beyond the one contradiction this card names.

## Report

Report to this issue first, then as your return message. Machine-checkable fields only — gates / line_budget / deviations / files_changed. Post your own `Claim:` comment (session ID + branch) in addition to this one. ⛔ Do not write the assignee field. `premise_still_valid: false` with `pr: null`, or `status: needs_decision` under Branch B, are both fully legitimate deliveries — Branch B is arguably the *more* valuable outcome, since it would mean a supported call shape has been refused by the type the whole time.

## ACCEPT — PR #8039. Verified against the diff, ⛔ not against the report

`domain:ui` seat, `session_01QnpvbdoRisQdRAczkLwnf5`, R2. Reviewed 2026-09-06T12:40Z.

### Checklist

| item | reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR form | #8039 draft, base `main`, `Fixes #7842` ✅ |
| scope | 3 files, all `packages/plugin-view` + a changeset — exactly the declared surface ✅ |
| Branch taken | **A**, and the declaration is **untouched** in the diff (`dataSource: DataSource;` unchanged) ⇒ no accept set moved ⇒ `Clause-②: no` confirmed **by the diff**, not by assertion ✅ |
| Branch B | ⛔ not implemented, as instructed ✅ |
| `packages/app-shell` `ObjectView` (#7483) | untouched ✅ |
| changeset | **empty-frontmatter** form. Correct: the only published-source edit is a comment, so no bump is owed while the gate still sees a changeset ✅ |

### The measurement answered the card, and my hint was right for a reason I had not seen

`ObjectView` holds **no context read at all** — no `useContext`, no `SchemaRendererContext`, and, decisively, not `useElementDataSource`, which is how `@object-ui/react` spells this fallback for components that genuinely have one. Every read site guards rather than resolves.

⭐ **But the third possibility I flagged turned out to be the real story, in a form neither the card nor I anticipated: the sentence was MISFILED, not invented.** `ObjectViewRenderer` (`index.tsx`), the renderer registered for the `object-view` and `view` tags, really does `useContext(SchemaRendererContext)` and hands `ctx?.dataSource` into this prop. So a schema-driven host *does* get the provider's adapter; a TSX caller does not. The card framed this as "one of the two is wrong" — the truth is the sentence was true of a different component. That is a better answer than either branch.

### ⭐ Two test-design decisions worth keeping on record

**1. It refused to stub the context, and said why.** Every sibling `ObjectView.*.test.tsx` mocks `@object-ui/react` and replaces `SchemaRendererContext` with a fresh `React.createContext(null)`. Following that convention here would have been a **false green**: a future fallback would be written against the *real* context (directly or via `useElementDataSource`), and a provider built on a look-alike object is invisible to it — so the test would keep passing while the thing it guards was reintroduced. This file keeps the real provider and real context and stubs only `SchemaRenderer`. ⛔ Do not "align it with its siblings" later.

**2. The negative is fronted by a live control, with the reason written into the failure message.** The interesting assertion is *"the context adapter is never touched"*, and a negative asserted alone is indistinguishable from a harness that could not observe the call at all. So the first case proves the same probe DOES fire when the adapter arrives as the prop, and its message says: *until this passes, the assertions below measure nothing*. That is the lane's "a zero needs a control that fires" rule, implemented **inside the artifact** rather than in a report.

Plus a **type pin** that makes the widening loud: an `@ts-expect-error` on an omitted `dataSource`, so if the prop ever becomes optional the directive goes unused and `tsc` fails **TS2578 naming that line**. Ablated in both directions (behaviour pin → exactly one red with its named message; type pin → TS2578 plus TS2322 at `ObjectView.tsx:1870`), each mutation proven on disk and each restore proven by hash rather than exit code.

### Derived work — correctly NOT filed

`ObjectViewRenderer` hands `ctx?.dataSource ?? null` into a prop declared non-nullable, and nothing complains because `SchemaRendererContext` is typed `any`. ⭐ The dev **did not file a card**, because that is a downstream instance of **#7912** — open, `needs-user-decision`, and already stating that narrowing the seam is a public-contract change with its own blast radius. A second card would have duplicated it. It is pinned here as an observation and explicitly not endorsed. Correct call: dedupe against an existing decision card beats filing a twin.

⚠️ Also worth recording: Branch B would **not** have been a one-character change — `ObjectView.tsx:1870` forwards this value into `renderListView`'s required `dataSource` parameter. Anyone reading "just make it optional" should see that first.

### One note, not a rework

The prop's JSDoc grows to ~34 lines for a card whose fix is deleting one sentence. I asked for it — "the prose was wrong" is not a description of behaviour — and each block earns its place (the measurement, the misfiling, the absent-prop behaviour, the ⛔ against widening). ⚠️ But it is now the largest comment on that interface; if a future editor trims it, the ⛔ line and the misfiling paragraph are the two that must survive.

### Landing

CI convergence and landing are this seat's. Same rule as its siblings: every check green, with `Live E2E (informational)` excepted as **established base-red** (measured on `main` run 34017174769, job 101442890465, failing at "Start ObjectStack backend (published packages)"; carded #7990, no objectui-side fix portable).
